rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spatial construction for directly overhead and higher-place or upstairs meanings; the farther-upstream reading needs different wording.

example.english: The lamp is above my head.
example.jyutping: zaan2 dang1 hai2 ngo5 go3 tau2 soeng6 bin6

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for something physically higher or on top, including clothing worn over another layer and places farther north on a map.

example.english: I wear my jacket above my shirt.
example.traditional: 我件外套着喺件恤衫上便。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin6 ngoi6 tou3 zoek6 hai2 gin6 seot1 saam1 soeng6 bin6

rows.note: Use this for an amount or number that exceeds another amount or number.

example.english: There are above one hundred people sitting here.
example.traditional: 呢度坐咗多過一百個人。
example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 zo6 zo2 do1 gwo3 jat1 baak3 go3 jan4

rows.note: Use this for being higher, better, or superior in degree, quality, or rank rather than simply greater in quantity.

example.english: Their English level is far above mine.
example.traditional: 佢哋嘅英文水平高過我好多。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 ge3 jing1 man4 seoi2 ping4 gou1 gwo3 ngo5 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this for something higher or mentioned earlier on the same page, rather than for a physical location.

example.english: Look at the paragraph above; the answer is already written.
example.traditional: 你睇返上面嗰段，已經寫咗答案。
example.jyutping: nei5 tai2 faan2 soeng6 min6 go2 dyun6 ji5 ging1 se2 zo2 daap3 on3

rows.note: Use this when above means more than a stated number or amount.

example.english: Today's temperature is above thirty degrees.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 hei3 wan1 do1 gwo3 saam1 sap6 dou6
